LEAID=5002610 | Brighton School District, VERMONT | Step 1
============================================================
**Elaine Collins is the superintendent overseeing Brighton School District (NCES LEAID 5002610) for the 2025–2026 school year.[1]**

## District Overview
Brighton School District in Island Pond, Vermont, is a small regular public school district and a component of the North Country Supervisory Union (NCSU), operating Brighton Elementary School (PK-8) with about 110 students.[2][6] In Vermont supervisory unions, the superintendent serves as the top leader for component districts like Brighton, coordinating with the local principal.

## Leadership Details
Elaine Collins has been NCSU superintendent since July 2022, with her role confirmed as current in February 2026 state records and union websites.[1][2] No news indicates departure or interim replacement; she testified as superintendent in early 2026. The district's principal is Mari Goodridge (effective July 2025), succeeding Annsunee Swift, but the superintendent holds top authority for the 2025–2026 year (Aug 2025–Jun 2026).[3][6]

============================================================
**Dr. Matthew Cheeseman is the superintendent of Craven County Schools for the 2025–2026 school year (Aug 2025–Jun 2026), having assumed the role on February 1, 2026.[4][10]**

## Leadership Timeline
Dr. Wendy A. Miller resigned effective May 30, 2025, with Michelle Lee initially serving as Acting Superintendent.[2]  
Richard L. Stout, Jr. was appointed Interim Superintendent effective May 1, 2025, and continued into early 2026, followed briefly by Dr. Stuart Blount as Interim from January 1, 2026.[3][4]  
Dr. Cheeseman was approved December 16, 2025, took the oath January 12, 2026, and began full duties February 1, 2026, with a contract through 2029.[4][10]

## Current Status
As of February 24, 2026, district records list Richard L. Stout, Jr. on the Superintendent's Cabinet page but reflect his interim role ending per transition announcements; Dr. Cheeseman leads through the 2025–2026 year.[10]

============================================================
Based on my research, **Sherry Sousa is the superintendent of Mountain Views Supervisory Union (which includes Mountain Views Unified Union School District #76) for the 2025–2026 school year.** [1] Sousa has served in this role for the past four years and continues to lead the district. [1]

## Leadership Background

Sherry Sousa has dedicated her career to working with adolescents with disabilities and has held various capacities within Mountain Views Supervisory Union. [1] Under her leadership, the district reimagined the role of special educators as Learning Specialists, which reduced the number of students receiving special education services from 17% to 11%. [1] She is committed to improving educational equity and sees literacy as a key component of that work. [1]

## Recent District Activity

In August 2025, Mountain Views Supervisory Union voted unanimously to join a Board of Cooperative Education Services (BOCES) with seven other supervisory unions and districts, making it the first supervisory union in Vermont to do so. [4] Superintendent Sousa has been meeting with her counterparts for the past five years to develop this collaborative structure that shares services in special education and professional development. [4]

Based on my research of Orrville City Schools' district website and official records, **Dr. David Toth** is the superintendent for the 2025–2026 school year [4][7][10].

## Superintendent Background

Dr. Toth began his educational career as a special education teacher and girls' basketball coach at Riverside Campus in Painesville, Ohio, and later served as Assistant Principal and Principal there [4]. He subsequently worked as High School Principal at West Geauga High School in Chesterland, Ohio, before becoming superintendent of Crestwood Schools in Mantua, Ohio [4]. He started his tenure at Orrville City Schools on August 1, 2024 [1], replacing Jon Ritchie, who had served as superintendent for many years.

## Current Status

Dr. Toth is actively serving as superintendent in February 2026, as evidenced by his recent "Info Page" update published on February 19, 2026 . The district website confirms he continues in this role for the 2025–2026 school year [7][10].

LEAID=5000412 | Caledonia Cooperative Unified School District #78, VERMONT | Step 1
============================================================
Based on my research, I found definitive information about the superintendent of Caledonia Cooperative Unified School District #78 in Vermont.

**Matthew Foster** is the superintendent of Caledonia Central Supervisory Union (CCSU), which includes Caledonia Cooperative Unified School District #78 in Danville, Vermont for the 2025–2026 school year. [4] This information is confirmed by the Vermont Agency of Education's official snapshot (updated February 2, 2026), which lists Matthew Foster as the superintendent. [4]

Foster has a long career in education, including roles as an elementary and middle school teacher, college instructor, assistant principal, principal, and executive director of business in Illinois before relocating to Vermont, where he served as principal at Wolcott and Craftsbury Schools. [1]

**Wil Cwikiel is the superintendent (also serving as principal) of Beaver Island Community School for the 2025–2026 school year.** [1][7][1]

## District Overview
Beaver Island Community School (NCES LEAID 2604350) is a small, single-school public district in Beaver Island, Michigan, serving Pre-K through 12th grade with around 50 students. [2][6] As a non-supervisory union district, the top leader holds dual superintendent/principal roles, consistent with its size. [3][5]

## Leadership Confirmation
The official district website lists Wil Cwikiel as Superintendent/Principal, alongside the 2024-2025 board and meeting schedules extending into mid-2025. [1][1] The homepage features his welcome message as Superintendent-Principal, with no updates indicating changes. [7][2] Recent news from August 2025 and December 2025 refers to him as principal/superintendent without mention of departure or replacement. [6]

No evidence of superintendent changes, interim leaders, or new appointments for 2025-2026 appears in Michigan state records, district pages, or news searches.

LEAID=3700421 | Catamount School, NORTH CAROLINA | Step 1
============================================================
Based on my research, I need to clarify the organizational structure:

**The Catamount School is a university lab school operated by Western Carolina University in partnership with Jackson County Public Schools.** It is not a traditional school district with its own superintendent. [2][1]

The Catamount School has a **Principal (Angela Lunsford)** and a **Superintendent role at the university level (Kim Winter, Dean of WCU's College of Education and Allied Professions).** [1] Kim Winter is identified as the "superintendent of the Catamount School" in the WCU context, as she oversees the school's operations as part of her role managing the university's lab school. [1]

However, for the broader **Jackson County Public Schools district** (which provides transportation and food services to The Catamount School), **Dr. Dana L. Ayers is the Superintendent.** [2]

Since your query specifies "Catamount School" with NCES LEAID 3700421 and identifies it as a "Regular public school district," and given that very small/single-school districts may have the principal as the top leader:

---

**DISTRICT_CONFIRMED:** The Catamount School  
**SUPERINTENDENT_FULL_NAME:** Angela Lunsford (Principal) or Kim Winter (University Superintendent)  
**CONFIDENCE:** medium  
**CONFIDENCE_REASON:** The Catamount School is a university lab school, not a traditional public school district. Angela Lunsford serves as Principal; Kim Winter serves as university-level superintendent. The organizational structure is non-standard.  
**UNKNOWN_REASON:** The lab school's governance structure does not align with typical superintendent roles in traditional districts.

LEAID=5000438 | Mountain View Union Elementary School District #94, VERMONT | Step 1
============================================================
**Mountain View Union Elementary School District #94 is a small district with three elementary schools (Hardwick, Lakeview, and Woodbury), supervised by Orleans Southwest Supervisory Union (OSSU). It has no dedicated superintendent listed; leadership is provided by principals at each school. For the 2025–2026 school year (Aug 2025–Jun 2026), the top leaders are William Deiss (Principal, Hardwick Elementary), Beth Parker (Principal, Woodbury Elementary and Lakeview Early Education Center), and Katherine Gascoyne (Assistant Principal, Hardwick Elementary). [2][4][1]**

## Leadership Structure
The district employs a shared principal model across campuses, with Deiss and Parker handling primary responsibilities collaboratively. [4][1] OSSU's Superintendent Dr. David Baker oversees the supervisory union, including this district, as of early 2026 (with Rebecca Tatistcheff appointed to start July 1, 2026). [3][2][8]

## Current Status
No superintendent changes or new appointments affect the 2025–2026 school year; staff listings confirm principals as top on-site leaders. [9]
